chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jameel ibn Salih from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Basri from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever hears the Mu'adhdhin saying: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' and he says it in confirmation and counting it as a good deed, saying: 'And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' he is sufficient for him with these two testimonies against everyone who refused and denied, and he assists with them everyone who affirmed and testified, unless Allah forgives him with a forgiveness equal to the number of those who denied and rejected, and equal to the number of those who affirmed and testified.

key_terms.مُحْتَسِباً: Counting it as a good deed/intending reward

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for repeating the Shahada during the Adhan?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the profound spiritual economy of the Adhan, where a believer’s sincere repetition of the Shahada serves as a comprehensive proxy for the entire community. This act not only accrues reward equal to all who affirmed the faith but also offsets the penalty of those who denied it, illustrating the Shia concept of collective merit (Hasanat al-Jama'ah). It underscores the Mu'adhdhin’s role as a spiritual catalyst, linking individual devotion to the broader cosmic struggle between belief and disbelief.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Abdillah b. Ja’far al-Himyari from Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hassan b. Mahbub from Jameel b. Salih from al-Harith b. al-Mughira al-Basri from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“One who hears the Muezzin say: Ash-hadu allaa ilaaha illallaahu wa ash-hadu anna muh’ammadar rasoolullaah and testifies it for the sake of seeking reward from Allah by saying Wa anaa ash-hadu allaa ilaaha illallaahu wa anna muh’ammadar rasoolullaahi aktafee bihimaa a’n kulli man abaa wa jah’ada wa uee’nu bihimaa man aqarra wa shahid Almighty Allah forgives him with the forgiveness equal to those who testify in this way and those who don’t.”
